result.topic_en: Euler discusses when friction entirely stops outflow from a reservoir (castellum) given its height q relative to M/N, how to design an aqueduct for the maximum fountain jet, and gives a table of jet heights for various pipe diameters with q = 130 ft and b = 2500 ft.
result.transcription:
386 TENTAMEN THEORIAE

atmoſphaerae debetur, quae ſi maior minorue eſſet, numeri $M$ in eadem ratione augeri, vel diminui, deberent.

115. Hinc ergo ſtatim elucet, ſi altitudo caſtelli $q$ minor fuerit, quam $\frac{M}{N}$, aquam ex orificio $DD$ non eſſe egreſſuram, ſed eius motum a frictione penitus compeſci. Ita ſi ſit $n=100000$, ſaliens fons non dabitur, niſi ſit $q>\frac{3000}{4}$, ſeu $q>750$ ped. Viciſſim autem, ſi altitudo $q$ detur, vt aqua ſaltem effluat, debet eſſe $\frac{M}{N}<q$; cum igitur creſcente $n$ valor $\frac{M}{N}$ creſcat, hinc innoteſcet limes, infra quem valor ipſius $n$ ſubſiſtere debet.

116. Si locus caſtelli vna cum loco fontis ſit datus, et quaeratur is aquae ductus, quo fons ad maximam altitudinem aſſiliat; primo canalis a caſtello quantum fieri poteſt ſecundum lineam rectam dirigi debet; deinde vero deſiderio potiſſimum ſatisfiet, ſi canali maxima tribuatur amplitudo, quam circumſtantiae permittunt. Ex tabula enim apparet, altitudinem iactus inprimis ab amplitudine canalis pendere.

117. Quod quo exemplo perſpiciatur, ſit altitudo caſtelli $q=130$ ped. et diſtantia eius a fonte $b=2500$ ped. et pro variis canalis diametris altitudo iactus ſe ita habebit:

items.quote: ſi altitudo caſtelli $q$ minor fuerit, quam $\frac{M}{N}$, aquam ex orificio $DD$ non eſſe egreſſuram, ſed eius motum a frictione penitus compeſci.
items.english: If the height of the reservoir q is less than M/N, the water will not flow out of the orifice DD, but its motion will be entirely checked by friction.

items.quote: Si locus caſtelli vna cum loco fontis ſit datus, et quaeratur is aquae ductus, quo fons ad maximam altitudinem aſſiliat
items.english: If the location of the reservoir together with the location of the fountain is given, and the aqueduct is sought by which the fountain leaps to the greatest height

items.quote: Ex tabula enim apparet, altitudinem iactus inprimis ab amplitudine canalis pendere.
items.english: For it appears from the table that the height of the jet depends chiefly on the width of the pipe.
